what: The intent, top down, from the brief: story > rules > examples; each example names the surface it will touch, in the brief's words, so the join can find it. Written by startups.engineer, an agent, from the voice memo of 20 October 2026 and the initial prompt; accepted by nobody yet, so every node is 'proposed': true until Dinis reads it back. Section numbers refer to the transcript's timestamps.

stories.title: A person finds their startup through an interview

rules.rule: The next question depends on the last answer: a state machine, not a form.

examples.example: A person who picks 'I do not have a startup yet' is not asked for a sentence about the thing

rules.rule: Everything maps to one test: can it ship, can it reach users, now.

examples.example: The ship stage asks for the smallest version a stranger could use this week, the blocker and the cost

rules.rule: It works along the spectrum from no startup yet to a good plan that is not shipping.

examples.example: Five entries on the where stage, each with its own route in

rules.rule: The finder does not pass judgement; it helps with focus and shipping; the output is in the person's words.

examples.example: The record's focus line is the person's; the interviewer may draft and must mark the draft
A capital-first startup gets the old-school route, said plainly, with next steps

stories.title: The same guidance works for a person on the site and for a model running the interview

rules.rule: One data file serves every surface.

examples.example: finder.json is published at finder/finder.json and the prompt names it
The stages and routes pages print the file's contents with ids

rules.rule: For now the finder is run by Claude or ChatGPT; the primitives come first, the programmatic version later.
